conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi Ms. ___, I’m Dr. ___. You were brought in after your dialysis because your blood pressure dropped quite low. Do you remember what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I felt a bit off after dialysis. I was nauseous and had been vomiting. They said my blood pressure was really low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s right. You were also running a fever and had a productive cough. We’re concerned you might have an infection. We’ve started antibiotics and fluids, but your blood pressure didn’t improve much, so we’ve started a medication called levophed to support it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. Is it serious? I’ve had low BP before after dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This is more serious than usual. Your labs show a severe infection in your blood — Klebsiella — and your body is struggling to keep up. We’re moving you to the ICU for closer monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Klebsiella? I’ve had infections before… but this sounds worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, this is septic shock. We think the infection started in your bile ducts. Your CT scan showed stones blocking the duct, which can cause a dangerous infection called cholangitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My bile duct? But I’ve had that groin abscess — could that be it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The abscess is healing well, and the CT showed no new infection there. But your bile duct is dilated and full of stones. That’s likely where the bacteria came from.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what happens now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll place a temporary drain in your bile duct to relieve the blockage and let the infection drain out. Then, once you’re stable, we’ll do a procedure called ERCP to remove the stones and place a stent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Last night, we placed a biliary drain. You’re now on strong antibiotics — meropenem — to treat the Klebsiella. Your blood pressure is improving, and we’ve weaned off the levophed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. But I was intubated last night — why?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You developed respiratory failure due to the infection and your underlying lung issues. We had to support your breathing. You’re off the ventilator now and doing well on oxygen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I see. And the drain — will it stay in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Only temporarily. Once you’re stable, we’ll do the ERCP to remove the stones and take the drain out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood cultures now show no growth — that’s great. The antibiotics are working. But we found something else — a blood clot in your left leg, near your dialysis catheter.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A clot? But I’m on Coumadin!

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We held Coumadin for the procedures, so we’ve started a heparin drip to bridge you. Once your INR is therapeutic again, we’ll restart Coumadin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to stay on blood thinners?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for now. Given your history of clots and the current DVT, we’ll continue anticoagulation. The renal team agrees it’s safer to keep the catheter in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning your ERCP tomorrow. The goal is to remove the stones and place a stent so your bile can flow properly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be intubated again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, briefly. The anesthesiologist will keep you comfortable. After the procedure, we’ll monitor you in the ICU before extubating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The ERCP went well. We removed two stones and placed a stent in your bile duct. The drain will be removed soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Is the infection gone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are improving. We’ll finish a two-week course of meropenem. The bile culture still grew E. coli, but it’s sensitive to the antibiotic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We removed the biliary drain this morning. You’re now on oral antibiotics and will finish the IV course.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the clot?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR is now therapeutic. We’ve stopped the heparin and will continue Coumadin. You’ll need INR checks regularly after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing much better. Your breathing has improved, and you’re off supplemental oxygen at rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been itching a lot on my back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We think it’s a reaction to the bleached sheets. We’ve switched them and started a mild steroid cream. We also noticed a fungal rash in your groin — we’ll treat that with miconazole.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your repeat ERCP showed no retained stones. The stent is working well. You’ll return in a month to have it removed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. What about my dialysis line?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve converted it to a tunneled catheter — more stable for long-term use. It’s in the same spot but better secured.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. Hemoglobin is low, but we’re not concerned — it’s likely from the illness and dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been constipated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve increased your stool softeners. The senna should help. Drink plenty of fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re making great progress. We’re planning to move you to the floor tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I feel stronger.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your final blood cultures are negative. You’ve completed your antibiotic course.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the itching?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Much better. We’ll send you home with benadryl and Sarna lotion in case it flares up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve reviewed your discharge plan. You’ll go to extended care for a few weeks to regain strength.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see GI in one month to remove the stent. Your primary will manage your Coumadin and INR checks. And please follow up with GYN about the vaginal bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your wound culture from the dialysis site came back — no growth. No need for antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re almost ready to go. We’ve updated your medications — midodrine for blood pressure, and your insulin doses are back to normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my BIPAP?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please use it at night. It will help with your sleep apnea and breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We removed the last drain. You’re all set for discharge tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel so much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final check — your labs are stable. Hemoglobin is still low, but it’s expected. We’ll monitor it at the extended care facility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any restrictions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No heavy lifting. Keep the dialysis site clean. Watch for fever, pain, or redness — call your team if any.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared for discharge tomorrow. We’ll send all instructions to the facility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate everything you’ve done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did great. Focus on rest, dialysis, and follow-up. We’ll see you in a month for the stent removal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Today’s the day. We’ll finalize your discharge meds and send you off with instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and don’t hesitate to call if anything comes up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. See you in a month!

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Looking forward to it. Have a safe trip to the facility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re all set. Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Ms. ___.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: You too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll be in touch with the facility to ensure a smooth transition.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your care will continue seamlessly. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’m good. Just ready to rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Rest is exactly what you need.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: See you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. Stay well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a safe journey.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Ms. ___.
